title: Several Delivery Claims on One Customer Profile
content:
A customer may hold any number of Delivery Claims claims across orders, and one order may carry claims of different types — for example a Missing Item Claim and a Damaged in Transit Claim on different lines. There is no cap on the number of claims per customer.

A unit compensated on one claim is never compensated again on another claim or through a return.

## Basis Q&A

**Is there a ceiling on how many claims one customer may have open or decided?**
No. There is no maximum per customer; the rule sets none.

**Can one order carry more than one claim?**
Yes, provided the claims are of different types. Two claim types on different lines of the same order are both allowed.

**A unit was reshipped under a Damaged in Transit Claim. Can the same unit be refunded again under a Missing Item Claim, or through a return?**
No. A unit compensated on one claim is never compensated again, whether on another claim or through a return.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

An order of three lines — a coat, a scarf and boots. The scarf is missing and the boots arrive scuffed. A Missing Item Claim on the scarf line and a Damaged in Transit Claim on the boots line can both stand on the order. Once the boots are compensated on the damage claim, those same units are not compensated again on any other claim or by a return.
